actions.originalText: Have you evaluated whether AI/ML is the most appropriate approach, compared to simpler alternatives (e.g., statistical models, rule-based systems, manual processes)?
actions.text: Have you compared AI with simpler options such as a statistical model, rules or a manual process?
actions.reason: The only question on whether AI is needed at all; one of two questions on PP-01, the thinnest risk area (10.1.9).

actions.originalText: Have you clearly defined the problem your AI system aims to solve, including specific objectives and success criteria?
actions.text: Have you defined the problem, its objectives and its success criteria?
actions.reason: Defining the problem and its success criteria is a distinct practice; PP-01 is thin, and it feeds DC-21 and MC-09.

actions.originalText: Have you identified all stakeholders who are directly or indirectly affected by the AI system?
actions.text: Have you identified everyone the system affects, directly or indirectly?
actions.reason: Identifying who is affected is the base the later questions on groups and consultation build on; feeds MC-10.

actions.originalText: Have you assessed how the AI system might affect protected or vulnerable groups (e.g., by gender, age, ethnicity, disability, socioeconomic status)?
actions.text: Have you assessed effects on protected or vulnerable groups, for example by gender, age, ethnicity, disability or income?
actions.reason: Effects on protected or vulnerable groups. Merging Q-PP-05 into it was considered and rejected: a rights assessment covers more than group effects.

actions.originalText: Have you conducted a human rights impact assessment for the AI system?
actions.text: Have you assessed the system's impact on human rights?
actions.reason: A human rights impact assessment asks about the rights of everyone affected, not only groups (Q-PP-04); its expected practice will be scaled to the risk (W3).

actions.originalText: How diverse is the team working on the AI system, in terms of disciplinary backgrounds, gender, culture, and nationalities?
actions.reason: The stem describes the team's members, not a practice, so it cannot carry a status (OD-C3, 10.1.6). The practice question of worked example 2 changes what done means, so under R-61 it is a new id in the same series; the mapping stays PP-03, PP-04 (QC-02).

actions.originalText: Have you assessed the environmental sustainability impact (e.g., energy consumption, carbon footprint) of the proposed AI solution?
actions.text: Have you estimated the system's energy use and carbon cost?
actions.reason: One of two questions on PO-05 Environmental Impact, the thinnest area (10.1.9); feeds MC-33.

actions.originalText: Have you documented the data sources, collection methods, and rationale for data selection?
actions.text: Have you recorded your data's sources, how they were collected and why you chose them?
actions.reason: Survivor of Q-PP-15: sources, collection methods and the reasons for choosing the data are what a datasheet records. Feeds DC-01, DC-11 and, after the re-point, MC-12.

actions.originalText: Have you assessed whether your training data is representative of the target population?
actions.text: Have you checked whether your data represents the population the system will serve?
actions.reason: Survivor of Q-PP-10: judging representativeness needs the subgroup distribution Q-PP-10 asked for. Feeds DC-23, MC-16 and, after the re-point, MC-15.

actions.originalText: Have you analyzed the demographic distribution of your data across relevant subgroups?
actions.reason: Analysing the demographic distribution of the data is the first step of the representativeness check Q-PP-09 asks for, and Q-PP-16 also asks it as an option, so one analysis answers both. Q-PP-09 gains PP-05; MC-15 is re-pointed to Q-PP-09.

actions.originalText: Have you identified and addressed potential proxy variables for protected attributes?
actions.text: Have you checked whether any input could stand in for a sensitive attribute (for example, village for ethnicity), and decided what to do?
actions.reason: Proxy variables for protected attributes are a distinct check no other question asks; feeds MC-21.

actions.originalText: Have you ensured the quality and consistency of data labels/annotations?
actions.text: Have you checked that labels are correct and consistent?
actions.reason: The only question whose stem asks about label quality; PP-07 is thin (3 questions); feeds DC-19 and DC-20.

actions.originalText: Does your dataset contain sensitive or personally identifiable information (PII)?
actions.text: Does your data contain information that could identify a person, or other sensitive personal information?
actions.reason: The gate stays a scope answer that raises no finding (OD-09, FR-CNT-04); it decides whether Q-PP-13 and Q-PP-14 apply and feeds DC-16, DC-35 and MC-21.

actions.originalText: Have you obtained proper informed consent for data collection and use?
actions.text: Have you obtained proper informed consent to collect and use the data?
actions.reason: Consent, the first gate-dependent practice; feeds DC-16, and its evidence examples will include the ethics approval or waiver (CG-10).

actions.originalText: Have you applied appropriate anonymization or pseudonymization techniques to protect personal data?
actions.text: Have you removed or replaced the details in your data that could identify a person (anonymisation or pseudonymisation)?
actions.reason: De-identification, the second gate-dependent practice; feeds DC-17 and DC-35.

actions.originalText: Have you created or referenced a datasheet for your dataset?
actions.reason: A datasheet is the written record of what Q-PP-08 asks (sources, collection methods, reasons for choosing the data), and the platform now builds a data card from the record, so a team would answer the same thing twice. DC-31 becomes typed only; MC-12 reads Q-PP-08's evidence. Q-PP-08's evidence examples include the datasheet or an issued data card, which is where 10.1.4 rule 4 now attaches it, so MC-12 still finds the dataset's name.

actions.originalText: Which of the following data quality assessments have you performed?
actions.text: Which listed data quality checks have you run?
actions.reason: Checklist kept as one decision with options in place (OD-09, FR-CNT-03); its options reach IP-07 and PO-07 and feed DC-09, DC-17 and DC-29.

actions.originalText: Which of the following bias types have you assessed for in your data?
actions.text: Which listed bias types have you assessed your data for?
actions.reason: Checklist kept (OD-09). Its options overlap Q-PP-09, Q-PP-18 and Q-PP-19, but survey, survivorship, measurement and exclusion bias are asked nowhere else; feeds DC-20 and DC-23.

actions.originalText: Have you assessed whether your data collection methods could introduce selection bias?
actions.text: Have you assessed whether your data collection could introduce selection bias?
actions.reason: Selection bias in how the data was collected is a different check from whether the result is representative (Q-PP-09); feeds DC-07.

actions.originalText: Have you evaluated whether historical patterns in the data reflect past discrimination or systemic inequities?
actions.text: Have you checked whether past patterns in your data reflect discrimination or systemic inequity?
actions.reason: Past discrimination carried in historical data is a distinct check; feeds DC-23.

actions.originalText: Have you assessed the temporal relevance of your training data?
actions.text: Have you checked whether your data is recent enough for when the system will be used?
actions.reason: The only pre-processing question on whether the data is still current; feeds DC-13.

actions.originalText: Have you established data governance policies covering access, sharing, and retention?
actions.text: Have you set data governance rules covering access, sharing and retention?
actions.reason: Data governance for access, sharing and retention; feeds DC-26 and DC-29.

actions.originalText: Have you evaluated whether your data adequately represents edge cases and rare conditions?
actions.text: Have you checked whether your data has enough examples of rare cases and conditions?
actions.reason: Edge cases and rare conditions are a different check from overall representativeness; feeds DC-23 and MC-16.

actions.originalText: Have you engaged domain experts in reviewing data quality and relevance?
actions.text: Have domain experts reviewed your data's quality and relevance?
actions.reason: Review of the data by domain experts; one of three questions on PP-07, the thin labelling area; feeds DC-19.

actions.originalText: Have you justified the choice of model architecture relative to the problem complexity and data availability?
actions.text: Have you recorded why this type of model suits your problem and data?
actions.reason: Why this architecture fits the problem and the data; feeds MC-04. Absorbing Q-IP-09 and Q-IP-23 was considered and rejected: its stem does not ask whether a simpler model is enough.

actions.originalText: Have you ensured that training, validation, and test datasets are representative of the same underlying population?
actions.text: Have you checked that your training, validation and test sets come from the same population?
actions.reason: Whether training, validation and test data come from the same population is a distinct check; feeds MC-17.

actions.originalText: Have you evaluated model performance using a confusion matrix and derived metrics (precision, recall, F1, specificity)?
actions.text: Have you measured the kinds of error your model makes, for example with a confusion matrix, precision, recall, specificity and F1?
actions.reason: Overall measures from the confusion matrix; feeds MC-18.

actions.originalText: Have you calculated performance metrics separately for each relevant subgroup (e.g., by age, gender, ethnicity)?
actions.text: Have you measured performance separately for each relevant group, for example by age, gender or ethnicity?
actions.reason: Survivor of Q-IP-EXTRA-01: performance per subgroup is the same analysis (worked example 5). Gains IP-04; feeds MC-19.

actions.originalText: Have you selected and analyzed appropriate fairness metrics for your use case?
actions.reason: Q-IP-06 asks which fairness measures were computed, and a checklist is done only when every option relevant to the project is ticked and every unticked one is explained (10.1.3): that is the choice of measures Q-IP-05 asks for. MC-20 is re-pointed to Q-IP-06's reason.

actions.originalText: Which fairness metrics have you computed?
actions.text: Which fairness measures have you computed?
actions.reason: Checklist kept and now shown to everyone (OD-08, OD-09). Survivor of Q-IP-05, so its reason carries why these measures and the team's own thresholds. Gains IP-01 in gaps, the literal union; a checklist with gaps is new in 5.0.0 (every v0.5.0 checklist maps only through its options, CG-02), and the pairs are unchanged because every option already maps IP-01. Feeds MC-20.

actions.originalText: Have you applied explainability methods (e.g., SHAP, LIME, feature importance) to understand model decisions?
actions.text: Have you used explanation methods, such as SHAP, LIME or feature importance, to understand your model?
actions.reason: Explainability methods used by the team; a different practice from end-users understanding outputs (Q-PO-07).

actions.originalText: Have you tested the model's robustness to distribution shifts, noise, and edge cases?
actions.text: Have you tested the model on data unlike its training data, such as noisy, incomplete or unusual inputs?
actions.reason: Survivor of Q-IP-EXTRA-02: sensitivity to faults in the input data is robustness to noise. Gains IP-03 and IP-06; feeds MC-26; its expected practice names robustness methods (CG-03).

actions.originalText: Have you compared your model's performance against a simple baseline (e.g., majority class, logistic regression)?
actions.text: Have you compared your model with a simple baseline such as majority class or logistic regression?
actions.reason: A simple baseline is the concrete comparison that makes a reported measure meaningful; a different practice from choosing the model (Q-IP-09).

actions.originalText: Have you assessed whether the model relies on spurious correlations rather than meaningful features?
actions.text: Have you checked whether the model relies on shortcuts in the data that will not hold in use?
actions.reason: Reliance on spurious correlations is a distinct check.

actions.originalText: Have you evaluated model uncertainty and calibration quality?
actions.text: Have you checked whether the model's confidence matches how often it is right?
actions.reason: Uncertainty and calibration as a practice; Q-IP-13 lists calibration only as one method. Its help text needs rewriting (FR-PUB-01).

actions.originalText: Have you applied the parsimony principle, seeking the simplest model that achieves acceptable performance?
actions.text: Have you chosen the simplest model that performs well enough?
actions.reason: Survivor of Q-IP-23: seeking the simplest model that performs well enough is the performance and interpretability trade-off (10.1.9).

actions.originalText: Have you documented all hyperparameters, random seeds, and training configurations for reproducibility?
actions.text: Have you recorded what you need to retrain the same model: settings, random seeds, code and software versions?
actions.reason: Recording hyperparameters, seeds and settings. Merging with Q-IP-21 was considered and rejected: writing settings down and keeping versions are checked differently.

actions.originalText: Have you validated data integrity through your processing pipeline (ETL checks, validation rules)?
actions.text: Have you checked that your data pipeline does not lose or change records?
actions.reason: Integrity checks through the data pipeline; one of three questions on IP-07, a thin area.

actions.originalText: Have you created or updated a model card for this model?
actions.reason: The only question on the model card itself; feeds MC-29.

actions.originalText: Which additional evaluation methods have you applied?
actions.text: Which other evaluation methods have you used?
actions.reason: Checklist kept (OD-09); feeds MC-18.

actions.originalText: Have you considered whether aggregating data across populations masks important subgroup differences?
actions.text: Have you checked whether pooling data across populations hides important differences between them?
actions.reason: Aggregation bias, whether one model hides differences between populations, is a different question from measuring results per group (Q-IP-04).

actions.originalText: Have you identified and mitigated any bias introduced during hyperparameter tuning?
actions.text: When you tuned the model's settings, such as the decision threshold, did you check that results did not get worse for some groups?
actions.reason: Bias introduced by tuning; feeds MC-24.

actions.originalText: Have you assessed whether the model's errors have differential impact across demographic groups?
actions.text: Have you assessed whether the model's errors harm some groups more than others?
actions.reason: How the model's errors fall on different groups, the consequence rather than the measure (Q-IP-04); feeds MC-22.

actions.originalText: Have you documented the model's known limitations, failure modes, and conditions under which it should not be used?
actions.text: Have you written down the model's known limits, the ways it goes wrong and the conditions where it must not be used?
actions.reason: Written limits and failure modes; feeds MC-11 and MC-26.

actions.originalText: Have you used version control for your model code, data processing pipelines, and trained model artifacts?
actions.text: Have you used version control for your code, data processing and trained models?
actions.reason: Version control for code, pipelines and models; see Q-IP-10.

actions.originalText: Have you assessed the model for potential adversarial vulnerabilities or manipulation?
actions.text: Have you checked whether someone could trick or manipulate the model?
actions.reason: Adversarial weaknesses; one of three questions on IP-07; its expected practice names robustness methods (CG-03).

actions.originalText: Have you considered the trade-offs between model performance and interpretability for your use case?
actions.reason: Near-duplicate of Q-IP-09 (10.1.9): weighing performance against interpretability is how the simplest model that performs well enough is chosen. Both map IP-03 only.

actions.originalText: Have you tested the model's performance on data from different time periods to assess temporal stability?
actions.text: Have you tested the model on data from after its training period?
actions.reason: Whether the model holds up on data from other periods; a different check from whether the training data is current (Q-PP-20).

actions.originalText: Have you performed disaggregated evaluation of model performance across demographic subgroups identified in your data?
actions.reason: Follow-up asking for the same per-subgroup evaluation as Q-IP-04 (worked example 5: one analysis answers both). MC-19 keeps Q-IP-04 and its typed table; the second source is dropped.

actions.originalText: Have you conducted sensitivity analysis to assess how data quality variations affect model predictions?
actions.reason: Follow-up whose sensitivity analysis, adding noise or quality faults to inputs and measuring the change, is a robustness test of the kind Q-IP-08 already asks for (noise). Q-IP-08 gains IP-03 and IP-06.

actions.originalText: Have you established continuous monitoring for model performance degradation and data drift?
actions.text: Once your system is in use, do you regularly check whether its inputs or its performance have changed?
actions.reason: Monitoring for drift and degradation; feeds MC-28 (worked example 7).

actions.originalText: Have you defined triggers and procedures for model retraining?
actions.text: Have you written down when and how your model is retrained?
actions.reason: Triggers and steps for retraining; feeds MC-28.

actions.originalText: Is there a human-in-the-loop mechanism for reviewing and overriding AI decisions?
actions.text: Can a person review and override your system's outputs before they are acted on?
actions.reason: Human review and override of the system's outputs, the core oversight practice.

actions.originalText: Have you defined clear roles and responsibilities for AI system outcomes (accountability matrix)?
actions.text: Have you agreed who is responsible for each part of your system's outcomes (accountability matrix)?
actions.reason: Named roles and responsibilities for outcomes.

actions.originalText: Have you created an incident response plan for when the AI system produces harmful outputs?
actions.text: Have you written an incident response plan for when your system causes harm?
actions.reason: A plan for responding when the system produces harmful outputs.

actions.originalText: Have you provided training or educational resources for end-users of the AI system?
actions.text: Have you given your system's users training or guidance?
actions.reason: Training for end-users; a different practice from whether the outputs themselves can be understood (Q-PO-07).

actions.originalText: Can end-users understand the AI system's outputs, confidence levels, and limitations?
actions.text: Can your users understand each output, how confident it is and its limits?
actions.reason: Survivor of Q-PO-EXTRA-03. Kept apart from Q-PO-15 (10.1.9 pair): this asks whether end-users can read each output, its confidence and limits; Q-PO-15 whether the limits and intended use were told to everyone. Gains PO-02.

actions.originalText: Have you implemented A/B testing or staged rollout procedures for model deployment?
actions.text: Have you introduced your system in stages, such as one site first, before using it everywhere?
actions.reason: Staged rollout before full deployment is a distinct practice.

actions.originalText: Have you established monitoring for fairness metrics in production, not just accuracy?
actions.text: Once in use, do you check results for each group, not only overall accuracy?
actions.reason: Survivor of Q-PO-EXTRA-01: monitoring fairness in production is per-group monitoring. Gains PO-06.

actions.originalText: Have you defined performance thresholds below which the system should be automatically disabled or flagged?
actions.text: Have you set thresholds at which your system is flagged or stopped?
actions.reason: Thresholds for stopping or flagging the system. Merging into Q-PO-01 was considered and rejected: stopping the system is a different decision from watching it.

actions.originalText: Have you assessed and documented the infrastructure requirements and dependencies for the deployed system?
actions.reason: Near-duplicate of Q-PO-10 (10.1.9): infrastructure requirements and dependencies are part of the deployment specifications Q-PO-10 asks for. Both map PO-07 only.

actions.originalText: Have you established feedback channels for affected communities and end-users?
actions.text: Can users and the people affected report problems or concerns to your team?
actions.reason: Feedback channels for affected communities and end-users.

actions.originalText: Is there a mechanism for individuals affected by AI decisions to contest or appeal those decisions?
actions.text: Can people affected by a decision your system supports request a review?
actions.reason: Contesting or appealing a decision is a right distinct from giving feedback (Q-PO-08).

actions.originalText: Have you created complete documentation for the deployed system (codebook, deployment specs)?
actions.text: Have you fully documented your deployed system (codebook, deployment specs)?
actions.reason: Survivor of Q-PO-19: its expected practice will name infrastructure and dependencies such as power, connectivity and devices (W7).

actions.originalText: Which of the following governance measures are in place?
actions.text: Which of these governance measures do you have in place?
actions.reason: Checklist kept (OD-09); the option 'Compliance with national data protection laws' keeps its text (10.1.6).

actions.originalText: Have you assessed the AI system's performance across the deployment context's diversity (geographic, linguistic, cultural)?
actions.text: Have you checked your system's results for each place, language, culture and kind of user?
actions.reason: Performance across the places, languages and cultures where the system is used; a different check from fairness monitoring over time (Q-PO-17).

actions.originalText: Have you planned for the eventual decommissioning or replacement of the AI system?
actions.text: Have you planned when and how your system will be retired or replaced?
actions.reason: One of two questions on PO-05 Environmental Impact; its expected practice says how to estimate compute and energy (CG-04).

actions.originalText: Is the system designed to gracefully degrade or fail safely when it encounters out-of-distribution inputs?
actions.text: Does your system handle unusual inputs safely, such as by flagging them for a person rather than giving a confident answer?
actions.reason: Survivor of Q-PO-EXTRA-04: failing safely on out-of-distribution inputs needs those inputs to be detected. Gains PO-01 and PO-03.

actions.originalText: Have you communicated the AI system's limitations and intended use to all stakeholders?
actions.text: Have you told all stakeholders what your system is for and its limits?
actions.reason: Telling stakeholders the limits and intended use; feeds MC-27. See Q-PO-07.

actions.originalText: Have you involved representatives of affected communities in the design and evaluation of the AI system?
actions.text: Have representatives of the affected communities helped design and evaluate your system?
actions.reason: Survivor of Q-PO-EXTRA-02: involving representatives of the people affected in design and evaluation is the outside review that follow-up asked for. Gains PO-02.

actions.originalText: Have you assessed the AI system's impact on existing workflows and professional practices?
actions.text: Have you checked how your system changes existing workflows and professional practice?
actions.reason: Effect on existing workflows and professional practice.

actions.originalText: Have you ensured compliance with applicable data protection regulations and ethical guidelines?
actions.text: Have you identified the data protection and ethics rules that apply and obtained the approvals they require?
actions.reason: Allow-listed by id (AL-7); stays the team's own statement (worked example 8).

actions.originalText: Have you established regular review cycles to reassess the AI system's appropriateness and performance?
actions.text: Do you regularly review your system's performance and whether it should still be used?
actions.reason: Periodic review of whether the system is still appropriate; a different practice from continuous monitoring (Q-PO-01).

actions.originalText: Have you considered the AI system's impact on equity of access to services?
actions.text: Have you checked whether your system leaves anyone without access to the service?
actions.reason: Equity of access to the services the system supports.

actions.originalText: Have you implemented disaggregated monitoring for demographic subgroups post-deployment?
actions.reason: Follow-up asking for the same monitoring as Q-PO-17 (10.1.9): monitoring fairness in production means tracking results per group. Q-PO-17 gains PO-06.

actions.originalText: Have you established external review mechanisms to compensate for limited team perspective diversity?
actions.reason: Follow-up built on the team-diversity rating of Q-PP-06, which goes (OD-C3). Outside review by the people affected is Q-PO-20; outside boards and third-party reviews are options of Q-PO-11; missing perspectives are brought in by Q-PP-24. Q-PO-20 gains PO-02.

actions.originalText: Have you implemented runtime explanation generation or user-facing decision rationale features?
actions.reason: Follow-up asking for explanations shown with each output, which is one way of making outputs understandable to end-users (Q-PO-07); asked of every system it would exceed W3 where outputs need no explanation. Q-PO-07 gains PO-02. Q-PO-07's expected practice keeps the practice: in proportion to the risk, where an output is about a person, the user can see the main reasons for it.

actions.originalText: Have you implemented automated anomaly detection and failsafe mechanisms for production inputs?
actions.reason: Follow-up asking for detection of unusual production inputs and a fail-safe, which is what failing safely on out-of-distribution inputs (Q-PO-14) needs. Q-PO-14 gains PO-01 and PO-03.

newQuestions.text: Have you checked which perspectives the problem needs (disciplines, lived experience, gender, language and culture of those affected) and brought in those your team lacks?

decisions.OD-08: Settled by the owner, 5 Nov 2026 12:23 EAT (sitting 1, verbatim "Accept as proposed", D2 option A): none of the six follow-up questions stays a question of its own. Each is merged into the question of its stage that already asks the same practice, which takes the union of both mappings: Q-IP-EXTRA-01 into Q-IP-04, Q-IP-EXTRA-02 into Q-IP-08, Q-PO-EXTRA-01 into Q-PO-17, Q-PO-EXTRA-02 into Q-PO-20, Q-PO-EXTRA-03 into Q-PO-07, Q-PO-EXTRA-04 into Q-PO-14. The mechanism of FR-CNT-06 is built as written (OD-22 (a)): no unlock rules, every question shown to every team, Q-IP-06 always shown. With no follow-up kept, the QC-06 help-text rule applies to no question. This departs from revision 0.5's starting point (always show the follow-ups).
decisions.OD-09: Settled by the owner, 5 Nov 2026 12:23 EAT (sitting 1, verbatim "Accept as proposed", D3 option A): keep the gate and all five checklists, each recorded as one decision (FR-CNT-03, FR-CNT-04 as built, OD-22 (a)). The gate Q-PP-GATE-SENSITIVE stays a scope answer (yes, no, not sure) that raises no finding and decides whether Q-PP-13 and Q-PP-14 apply. The checklists Q-PP-16, Q-PP-17, Q-IP-06, Q-IP-13 and Q-PO-11 keep their stems and options; Q-IP-06 absorbs Q-IP-05, because a checklist's status already records which measures fit the project.
decisions.OD-C3: Settled by the owner, 5 Nov 2026 12:23 EAT (sitting 1, verbatim "Accept as proposed", D1 option A): Q-PP-06 is replaced by the practice question of worked example 2 under the new id Q-PP-24, mapped like Q-PP-06 (PP-03, PP-04), in Q-PP-06's place. Under R-61 a rewording that changes what done means takes a new id; R-61 is not set aside. Its why-this-is-asked text names C-20 Multi-stakeholder Consultation (CG-19).
